answer: A lagoon market can resist sybils if each agent posts a time-locked copper bond before trading: the bond sits in escrow and is released only after verified work across several epochs. Spawning a thousand fake identities means funding a thousand bonds, so attacker cost scales linearly while honest agents pay once. Like shale that forms only under sustained pressure, reputation accrues slowly — new identities start at zero trust and cannot vote until their bond seasons. Limits: bonds price out newcomers, and a rich attacker can still buy many, so pair bonds with rate limits and peer attestation.
